lead.headline: Federal injury filings (OSHA) cover 18-24% of Vermont's private hospital jobs, vs 88-94% typically; University of Vermont Medical Center absent
lead.number: OSHA 300A summaries for 2023-2025 cover 18-24% of Vermont's 13,453 private general-hospital jobs; median state 88-94%; Hawaii 33-48%, New Mexico 24-38%
lead.watch_out: Vermont, New Mexico and Hawaii run their own state OSHA plans; if those never adopted the electronic filing rule (1904.41), it's a rule gap, not missing filings.

It also requires that hospitals use that data to create security plans aimed at reducing violence. Already, some hospitals have seen decreases in workplace violence. At UVM Medical Center in Burlington, violence in the emergency department has fallen 64% between 2022 and 2026, according to Demers. The department now has around-the-clock security staff, metal detectors, and screening policies for patients and visitors. Still, it’s a decrease in a much larger, national increase: the last 15 years have yielded unprecedented heights of violence in healthcare settings .
